title: A Wolf for the Salt
premise: Theo Almeida keeps the ledgers of the Salt Guild, which trades in impossible things — bottled storms, borrowed years, names that were never spoken. When the old gods begin answering prayers again, every debt in his ledgers comes due at once, and Theo discovers he is himself an entry: a man written into existence by a god who needed a witness. To escape a country that is being unmade by divine memory, he must find the Door of Salt, the one exit from Vessany, a nation erased from every map but its own. In the end Theo chooses to stay long enough to rewrite the ledger itself, trading his own recorded life to restore Vessany's name — and walks out through the Door as both its author and its ghost.
about_author: Silas Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about bureaucracy, belief, and the violence of forgetting.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Theo Almeida audits the Salt Guild's vaults, cataloguing bottled storms and unspoken names. POV: Theo. He notices one entry in his own handwriting he cannot remember writing: his own name, dated tomorrow. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine competence.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered in the Fish Market
chapters.summary: In the harbor city of Brineholt, a fishwife's prayer is answered by something vast and old; three blocks flood with sweet water. POV: Theo, investigating for the Guild. Beat: wonder curdling into dread as the gods' return breaks the rules of trade.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Years
chapters.summary: A dying woman pays the Guild thirty years of her life to hear her dead son's voice once more. Theo brokers the deal and hears the son say Theo's own name. POV: Theo. Beat: guilt — the trade worked, and it was meant for him.

chapters.title: Vessany, Which Is Not on Any Map
chapters.summary: Following the ledger anomaly, Theo crosses a border that appears only at dusk into Vessany, a country erased from every atlas yet crowded with living people. POV: Theo. Beat: vertigo and reluctant awe at a nation sustained purely by memory.

chapters.title: The Cartographer Who Drew Herself Out
chapters.summary: Theo meets Ilsa Vane, a cartographer exiled for mapping Vessany accurately — an act the erasure punishes. She recognizes his ledger as a god's instrument. POV: Ilsa. Beat: wary alliance; she needs him, he needs her maps.

chapters.title: Debts Come Due
chapters.summary: Every impossible thing the Guild ever sold reverts as the old gods reclaim their power; buyers age, storms escape bottles, names unravel their owners. POV: Theo. Beat: panic and responsibility — his ledgers are the index of the catastrophe.

chapters.title: The God Who Needed a Witness
chapters.summary: In a drowned chapel, the god Ossuin reveals the truth: Theo was written into being to record Vessany's final days, because a thing witnessed cannot be wholly erased. POV: Theo. Beat: identity shattered — he is ink, not flesh.

chapters.title: Salt on the Tongue
chapters.summary: Ilsa tests Theo's nature with salt and old rites; he does not bleed like men do, but he remembers like gods do. POV: Ilsa. Beat: grief for the friend she was beginning to trust, and resolve to use him anyway.

chapters.title: The Unmaking Road
chapters.summary: Traveling toward the Door of Salt, they pass villages dissolving into blank white silence where no one can recall them. POV: Theo. Beat: horror and urgency — time is literally running out behind them.

chapters.title: The Toll-Keeper's Bargain
chapters.summary: At a bridge of knuckle-bone, a toll-keeper demands a memory as payment. Theo pays with his mother's face and cannot afterward say why he weeps. POV: Theo. Beat: sacrifice begins; the cost of passage is selfhood.

chapters.title: What the Guild Knew
chapters.summary: They find the Guild's master, Corvane, alive inside a sealed vault of preserved hours — he foresaw everything and built the ledgers to cage the gods' debts. POV: Corvane. Beat: moral complexity — the villain's motive is mercy.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Corvane admits he commissioned Theo's creation and offers him freedom if Theo burns the ledgers, dooming Vessany but sparing the world. POV: Theo. Beat: temptation — survival offered at the price of complicity.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Map of Everything Lost
chapters.summary: Ilsa unveils her life's work: a map stitched from survivors' memories that could anchor Vessany permanently — if someone carries it through the Door and speaks it aloud outside. POV: Ilsa. Beat: hope, fragile and enormous.

chapters.title: Riot of the Remembered
chapters.summary: Vessany's capital erupts as citizens learn the truth of their erasure; the Guild's local house burns, and Theo saves the ledgers from the flames. POV: Theo. Beat: chaos, and clarity — the ledgers must be rewritten, not burned.

chapters.title: The Second Witness
chapters.summary: Ossuin's rival, the goddess Mereth of Tides, offers Theo a counter-deal: betray Ossuin and she will make him fully human. POV: Theo. Beat: longing for ordinary life warring with duty to the unwritten.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: Corvane's hunters ambush the party at the flats; Ilsa takes a wound meant for Theo, and her map is torn in half. POV: Ilsa. Beat: despair — the plan broken, the alliance bloodied.

chapters.title: Mending with Memory
chapters.summary: To repair the map, Theo feeds it pieces of his own recorded past; each fragment given makes him fainter. POV: Theo. Beat: bittersweet dissolution — becoming less so the country can become more.

chapters.title: The Door of Salt
chapters.summary: They reach the Door, a seam of white light guarded by Ossuin, who demands the map be left inside so Vessany dies witnessed rather than saved. POV: Theo. Beat: confrontation between maker and made.

chapters.title: The Rewriting
chapters.summary: Climax: Theo seizes the ledger-pen within himself and rewrites his own entry — striking his name, inscribing Vessany's — trading his existence for the nation's restoration as gods and Corvane converge. POV: Theo. Beat: defiant transcendence.

chapters.title: A Country With Its Name Back
chapters.summary: Vessany blazes back onto every map; its people wake remembering themselves. Ilsa stands at the border holding half a map and half a friend's memory. POV: Ilsa. Beat: triumph shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: The Man Outside the Ledger
chapters.summary: Outside the Door, a stranger with salt-white eyes wakes on a Brineholt dock with no past but a cartographer's instinct and a name no ledger holds. POV: Theo (unnamed). Beat: rebirth — justice achieved outside law, identity remade free.

chapters.title: Entries Pending
chapters.summary: Ilsa finds him; he doesn't know her, but he draws her harbor perfectly and asks what lies beyond the maps. Together they open a fresh ledger. POV: alternating. Beat: hopeful close — some things are worth beginning unwritten.
